name: Tallahassee, Florida, 15 September 2004 (evening balloon)
line: Very moist tropical air with strong wind shear near the ground (20 m/s in the lowest 1 km).
note: The balloon launched at 0000 UTC on 16 September (8 pm local time on the 15th), in the outer rain bands of a hurricane coming ashore. The storm is started by a gentle push of rising air, as CM1's updraft nudging does. In a 1 km run the storms last the whole two hours (measured). This day's sounding in an idealized storm, not a reconstruction of that day's storms.

gm1_settings_why: The push of rising air that starts the storm is centred 10.2 km east and 0.1 km south of the centre, the storm-track check's recommended place for this sounding, so the storm keeps the most room to every side. CM1 keeps the nudging's centre in its code (xc_wnudge, yc_wnudge), not the namelist, so this is a GM1 setting.
